hero.headline: A Next.js animation library, built on GSAP.
hero.body: Annnimate is a library of {count} GSAP components you copy into a Next.js app. Each file starts with "use client" and cleans up when it unmounts, so your pages stay Server Components and nothing leaks between routes.

bodies: Pick React on a component's page and save its two files side by side.
Import it into any page, App Router or Pages Router. The page stays a Server Component.
Every setting is a prop. Tune it live on the component's page, then copy the values.

handled.headline: What breaks GSAP in Next.js is already handled.

rows.title: Route changes
rows.body: A ScrollTrigger from the last page keeps firing after you navigate.
rows.aside: Every component kills its timelines and ScrollTriggers when it unmounts.

rows.title: StrictMode
rows.body: In development React mounts each component twice, so a hand-written animation runs twice.
rows.aside: Cleanup runs between the two mounts, so you see one animation.

rows.title: Server Components
rows.body: A component with hooks can't render inside a Server Component page.
rows.aside: Each file starts with "use client". Import it into any page and the page stays on the server.

rows.title: Reduced motion
rows.body: Visitors who turned motion off in their system settings still get the full animation.
rows.aside: Every component checks prefers-reduced-motion and respects it.

faq.headline: Questions, answered.
faq.subtext: What Next.js developers ask before they copy a component.

items.q: Does Annnimate work with the Next.js App Router?
items.a: Yes. Every React component starts with "use client" and cleans up when it unmounts, so it works from any page in app/ and the page stays a Server Component. The Pages Router works too.

items.q: Do the animations break on route change?
items.a: No. Each component kills its timelines and ScrollTriggers when it unmounts, so nothing from the last page keeps running after you navigate.
Yes. Cleanup runs between StrictMode's two mounts in development, so you see one animation, not two.

items.q: Do I need to install GSAP separately?
items.a: Yes, once per project: gsap and @gsap/react. GSAP has been free for commercial use, every plugin included, since version 3.13. Each component's page lists the plugins it uses.

endCta.headline: Motion for Next.js, without the setup.

hero.headline: A Nuxt animation library, built on GSAP.
hero.body: Annnimate is a library of {count} GSAP components you copy into a Nuxt app as plain Vue files. Each one starts its animation in onMounted, which Nuxt only runs in the browser, and cleans up when you leave the page.

bodies: `npm install gsap`, once per project. No Nuxt module, no config change.
Pick Vue on a component's page and save its files in `components/`.
Import it into any page with its CSS. Nuxt renders the markup, the browser runs the animation.
Every setting is a prop. Tune it live on the component's page, then copy the values.

handled.headline: What breaks GSAP in Nuxt is already handled.

rows.title: Server rendering
rows.body: Code that reaches for window or the DOM during setup breaks the server render.
rows.aside: Each component starts its animation in onMounted, which Nuxt only runs in the browser.

rows.title: Page changes
rows.body: Leave a page and its ScrollTriggers keep measuring a layout that's gone.
rows.aside: Each component reverts its animation when it unmounts.

rows.title: Plugins
rows.body: A ScrollTrigger or SplitText call does nothing until the plugin is registered.
rows.aside: Each component imports and registers the plugins it uses.

rows.title: Reduced motion
rows.body: Visitors who turned motion off in their system settings still get the full animation.
rows.aside: Every component checks prefers-reduced-motion and respects it.

faq.headline: Questions, answered.
faq.subtext: What Nuxt developers ask before they copy a component.

items.a: Yes. The components are plain Vue 3 files with <script setup>. Import one into any page, layout or component. Each one starts its animation in onMounted, which Nuxt only runs in the browser.

items.q: Do I need a Nuxt module for GSAP?
items.a: No. Install gsap and import the component. There's no module to register and no nuxt.config change.

items.q: Do the animations survive page changes?
items.a: Yes. Each component reverts its animation when it unmounts, so nothing keeps running after you leave a page.
No. The markup renders on the server and the animation starts in the browser. Wrap a component in ClientOnly only if you want it to skip server rendering entirely.

endCta.headline: Motion for Nuxt, without the setup.
